To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long-term carrier-envelope phase stability of a laser with a grating based stretcher and compressor is as good as that with a glass-block stretchers and prism compressors and the relative CE phase can be locked to an arbitrarily value.

the CE phase of pulses from high power ultrafast lasers with grating-based chirped pulse amplifications can be stabilized to the same level as lasers with glass-block stretcher, prism pair compressor and hollow-core fiber compressor, and the CE phase can be adjusted to any value in the range 2pi.

a high-power ultrafast laser system based on chirped pulse amplifications with grating stretchers can have CE phase stabilization as good as that using glass-block stretcher, and that the CE phase can be controlled with a precision of a fraction of a radian by adjusting the grater separation in the stretchers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the CE phase stability of the pulses after a grating stretcher and compressor.
the development of a CE-phase stabilized laser system based on the grating-based compressor, which is more compact and robust compared with the glass-block stretcher-prism compressor system.
the development of a new CE phase control method, and the results are important for the applications of high power laser systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
grating-based stretchers and compressor are a good choice for CE-phase stabilization, and the method described here is a simple and effective way to achieve this.
the long term stability of the CE phase in grating-based chirped pulse amplifications can be as good or even better than that of a glass-block based stretcher.
CE phase stabilization of a grating-based system is possible, but is more challenging than a glass-block based system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CE phase of pulses from an ultrafast laser system can be controlled with high precision and accuracy.
we have demonstrated a new technique to control the CE phase in grating-based systems.
the CE phase of the pulses can be stabilized to an rms value of 180mrad by adjusting the grater separation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the grating based chirping technique is not a limiting factor for CE-phase control.
the grating-based chirped pulse amplifications systems are capable of producing stable and controllable carrier-envelope phase.
the CE phase of a laser system can be stabilized with a grating based compressor and a feedback control system.
